Incorporating the latest Financial Stability Report, the statement’s solid growth and low unemployment alongside “somewhat elevated” inflation still support a restrictive and patient stance. The FSR notes system resilience (strong bank capital/liquidity) but highlights vulnerabilities that argue for caution: persistent CRE stress at some banks, tighter credit in SLOOS, elevated asset valuations, run‑prone nonbank funding structures (MMFs, stablecoins), and tail risks from fiscal debt sustainability and geopolitics. Hedge fund leverage appears to have eased and non-agency issuance was strong earlier in 2024, but overall funding and market‑liquidity fragilities remain two‑sided risks. These stability considerations reinforce the Committee’s “balanced risks” and data dependence and modestly temper the growth‑positive tone.

Net tone: neutral with a slight positive tilt, but a bit more cautious than before.
